title: Development of two loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) genomics-informed diagnostic protocols for rapid detection of Pantoea species on rice
author: Kini, Wonni, et al.

steps.title: Collect and label plant samples
steps.instruction: Collect diseased rice leaves at heading‑to‑maturity stages, whether showing typical bacterial leaf blight symptoms or not, and also collect apparently healthy or symptomatic rice seeds (stored seeds may be used). Place each sample in a paper envelope, label the envelope with variety, location, sampling date, and rice ecosystem, transport to the laboratory, and keep the envelopes in a refrigerator.

steps.title: Surface sterilize tissue pieces
steps.instruction: Clean and air‑dry the collected leaves and grains, cut leaves into small pieces, sterilize them by immersing in a 1 % sodium hypochlorite solution, then rinse thoroughly with sterilized distilled water.

steps.title: Extract bacterial ooze
steps.instruction: Transfer the sterilized leaf pieces or seeds into 15‑ml conical polypropylene Falcon tubes containing 5–10 ml sterilized distilled water, incubate for 10–15 min at room temperature to allow bacteria to ooze out, seal the tubes with parafilm, and label the tubes with the same information as the envelopes. The bacterial ooze obtained is ready for downstream LAMP testing.

steps.title: Culture bacteria and prepare lysate
steps.instruction: Keep the tubes on ice in a cooler box, streak the aqueous bacterial ooze onto freshly prepared PSA or PGSA agar plates, label the plates, and incubate at 28 °C for 1–3 days. After incubation, scrape the bacterial growth from each plate, suspend the cells in nuclease‑free water pre‑aliquoted in LightCycler® 480 Multiwell Plate 96 or LightCycler® 8‑Tube Strips, then heat‑lyse by incubating at 95 °C for 45 min. Include the following reference strains as positive controls: Pantoea CFBP 466, CFBP 3612T, CFBP 3171PT, CFBP 3615PT, CFBP 3845T, CFBP 6627T, and Erwinia CFBP 6632. Include Burkholderia glumae, Pseudomonas spp., Sphingomonas spp., and Xanthomonas oryzae as negative controls.

substeps.instruction: Streak bacterial ooze onto PSA or PGSA agar plates and incubate at 28 °C for 1–3 days.
Scrape colonies and suspend in nuclease‑free water in LightCycler plates.
Add reference and negative‑control strains as indicated.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Use the Wizard Genomic DNA Purification Kit, following the manufacturer’s instructions, to isolate genomic DNA from the bacterial lysate. Evaluate DNA quality and quantity by agarose‑gel electrophoresis and spectrophotometry.
